description: Alterations and extension to nursery involving a front porch extension, hip to gable roof replacement, loft conversion with rear dormer and roof lights to front, garage conversion with front porch addition and the creation of one on street parking bay
decision_conditions: The development to which this permission relates must be commenced not later than three years from the date of this permission.
To comply with the requirements of Section 91 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 (as amended by Section 51 of the Planning and Compulsory Purchase Act 2004).
The development hereby permitted shall not be carried out otherwise than in complete accordance with the following approved drawings:
For the avoidance of doubt and to ensure that the development is carried out as approved.
All new external finishes shall be carried out in materials to match those of the existing building(s) to the satisfaction of the Local Planning Authority.
To safeguard the appearance of the premises and the character of the immediate area.

The loft space hereby approved shall be restricted to staff office and staff room use only and shall not be utilised as additional classroom or children's accommodation without the prior grant of express planning permission from the Local Planning Authority.

To ensure that the intensity of the nursery use does not increase beyond the assessed parameters, and to safeguard highway safety and local parking capacity from unmitigated travel demand, in accordance with Policies 23, and 24 of the Havering Local Plan and Policy T4 of the London Plan.

The operational measures and travel management procedures detailed in the submitted application documents, including the staggered pick-up/drop-off schedules, the Q-Bell digital handover system, staff-supervised handover protocols, and the measures outlined within the Travel and Traffic Management Plan, shall be permanently adhered to and implemented in full during the operational life of the nursery.

In the interests of highway safety, traffic flow, and the protection of residential amenity, ensuring that travel demand is actively managed to prevent congestion, in accordance with Policies 7, 23, and 24 of the Havering Local Plan and Policy T4 of the London Plan.

The development shall not be brought into use until the proposed on-street kerb-mounted parking bay on Winifred Avenue and the reconfigured on-site driveway drop-off/pick-up bays have been fully constructed and made operational in accordance with the approved plans. These spaces shall thereafter be permanently retained and kept available for their designated drop off/pick up of children only and not for general parking by staff to the premises.

To ensure that adequate parking and drop-off/ pick-up facilities are provided prior to the operation of the expanded facility, thereby safeguarding highway safety and preventing obstructive parking on the surrounding highway network, in accordance with Policies 23 and 24 of the Havering Local Plan, Policy SI 1 of the London Plan and relevant guidance, as subsequently amended.

1) a) If, during development, contamination not previously identified is found to be present at the site then no further development (unless otherwise agreed in writing with the local planning authority) shall be carried out until a remediation strategy detailing how this unsuspected contamination shall be dealt with has been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The remediation strategy shall be implemented as approved.

b) Following completion of the remediation works as mentioned in (a) above, a 'Verification Report' must be submitted demonstrating that the works have been carried out satisfactorily and remediation targets have been achieved.

To ensure that any previously unidentified contamination found at the site is investigated and satisfactorily addressed in order to protect those engaged in construction and occupation of the development from potential contamination.
The Nursery shall operate with no more than 60 children on site at any one time.
To enable the Local Planning Authority to retain control, to avoid disturbance to adjoining residents and in the interests of highway safety.

The premises shall not be used for the purposes hereby permitted other than between the hours of 07.00 and 19.00 hours on Mondays to Fridays and not at all on Saturdays, Sundays, Bank or Public holidays.
To enable the Local Planning Authority to retain control in the interests of amenity.

This planning permission strictly relates to the physical alterations and extensions approved. It does not convey approval for any increase in the maximum daily occupancy of children and staff or any alteration to the established operational hours of the nursery, without the prior grant of express planning permission from the Local Planning Authority.
